Apple introduces MacBook Pro with M5, M5 Pro and M5 Max

Published 2026-10-07 17:30 UTC

CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced the new 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro featuring the M5 family of chips: M5, M5 Pro and M5 Max. With a next-generation GPU that has a neural accelerator in each core, MacBook Pro with M5 delivers up to 45 percent faster graphics performance than the previous generation and dramatically faster on-device AI.

The Liquid Retina XDR display now delivers up to 1,600 nits of SDR brightness outdoors, and MacBook Pro offers up to 24 hours of battery life, the longest ever in a Mac. Every model includes three Thunderbolt 5 ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot and MagSafe 3.

Pricing and availability: the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 starts at $1,599 and the 16-inch model starts at $2,499. Customers can order today, with availability beginning Wednesday, October 15.

MacBook Pro with M5 features a Liquid Retina XDR display with up to 1,600 nits of peak brightness for SDR content outdoors and 1,000 nits sustained for HDR content. An optional nano-texture display reduces glare in bright environments. The 12MP Center Stage camera supports Desk View for video calls.

M5 Pro features up to a 14-core CPU and up to a 20-core GPU, with support for up to 64GB of unified memory. M5 Max features up to a 16-core CPU and up to a 40-core GPU, with up to 128GB of unified memory and 546GB/s of memory bandwidth. Every M5 chip includes a faster 16-core Neural Engine.

MacBook Pro features three Thunderbolt 5 ports, an HDMI port that supports 8K output, an SDXC card slot, a headphone jack and MagSafe 3 charging. Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 are standard across the lineup.

The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 starts at $1,599 and $1,499 for education. The 14-inch and 16-inch models with M5 Pro and M5 Max start at $1,999 and $2,499. Customers can order today on apple.com and in the Apple Store app in 30 countries and regions, with availability beginning next week. MacBook Pro is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure and 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and its packaging is entirely fiber-based.
